context.problem_statement: Estimate the cardinality (distinct count) of a high-cardinality column (user_session_id) in a large events table using approximate methods. Implement: (1) exact COUNT(DISTINCT) as ground truth, (2) HyperLogLog approximation using the Flajolet-Martin sketch (implement in Python as SQL is running on SQLite which lacks native HLL), (3) sampling-based estimation: estimate distinct count from a 10% random sample then scale up, (4) report relative error of each approximation. Also run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the exact COUNT(DISTINCT) query and identify the query plan bottleneck.
context.expert_knowledge: HyperLogLog error rate is approximately 1.04/sqrt(m) where m is the number of registers. PostgreSQL has pg_hll extension. Sampling estimate: distinct_in_sample * (1/sample_rate) overcounts; use capture-recapture correction. COUNT(DISTINCT) requires full table scan; for very large tables, approximate methods crucial. Alternative: ndistinct statistic in pg_stats after ANALYZE.
